Hi all,

Thanks for doing the loop on Priya yesterday. I pulled together the notes and a draft consolidated scorecard (attached) with per-interviewer numeric entries and quick bullets. High level: very strong infra design thinking and product sense; split opinions on low-level systems coding exercise and trade-off depth.

Attachments: Priya_Desai_Resume.pdf, priya_scorecard_draft.csv

Quick summary table (from draft):
- System design / scope: 8, 9, 7, 8
- Implementation / coding: 6, 7, 5, 6
- Impact / leadership: 8, 8, 8, 7
- Overall hire recommendation: 3x "Hire", 1x "Consider"

As requested earlier, I'm trying to get us to a single normalized score and a short rationale we can share with recruiting. Two asks:
1) If you disagree with any numeric cell in the attached, please reply with the corrected number and a 1-2 line reason.
2) If you have calibration context (e.g., you scored low because of timeboxing vs. content), put that in-line — we should avoid conflating style vs. competency.

Can folks reply by EOD Tuesday (4/27)? If not, flag your availability and we can set a 20m sync.

—Marissa

Thanks Marissa — quick notes inline.

On 25 Apr 2027, Marissa wrote: 
> - Implementation / coding: 6, 7, 5, 6

My vote on the 5: that was me. I scored lower because the coding exercise stalled on the fault-injection portion; Priya's approach was correct conceptually but she didn't get to a robust error-recovery plan under the time limit. I don't think it's a permanent deficiency — more an indication of needing a fuller pairing session. Recommend we mark coding as a 6 (I can be convinced either way).

Also: for System design, I gave an 8 but I'd like to call out that she brought up cross-region cache invalidation as a first-class concern, which is high signal for this role.

No objections to the hire recommendation — I lean Hire with a note to include a short pairing check on the coding exercise during bar-raising loop.

Thanks,
Maya

Agree with Maya on the cache invalidation point — that was a differentiator. My primary concern is consistency of scoring across interviewers. I'm attaching a short calibration note I used for the last round; I think we should normalize by interviewer mean to avoid variance-driven false negatives (I had one interviewer skew down overall).

Suggested next steps:
- Normalize scores by subtracting each interviewer's mean score across the four candidates in this funnel (quick spreadsheet step).
- Convert back to 1-10 scale and then produce a weighted average: system design (40%), implementation (30%), impact (20%), culture/communication (10%).

If we do that, my recalculated overall goes up ~0.6 points and keeps Priya comfortably above our bar. I'm +1 for hire pending the short pairing check.

Attachment: calibration_notes.docx

Jonas

1) Marissa — can you confirm recruiting's timeline? Priya asked; let's aim to close by Friday 5/1 if we can.

2) Calibration: Jonas' normalization approach makes sense to me.
